metadata.title: Resolve Standup Republic entities
metadata.description: Resolve an ambiguous human name, natural-language identifier, or supported provider identifier into stable SR references. For a dated performance, resolve an event; use show for its reusable template. Supply the narrowest plausible entity_types plus optional city/date/provider hints; full date_hint values are RFC3339. Connected resolver types depend on the current runtime adapter; use the live catalog and its connected types. Unconnected types return resolver_entity_type_not_connected with connected_entity_types. Use sr_entity_get when a canonical ref is already known; slot is a bookable lineup time window and is normally queried with available_slots_v1. Read-only; do not probe unsupported types.

query.description: Human text, name, message excerpt, phone number, email, or provider identifier to resolve into canonical SR references.

entity_types.description: Explicit plugin entity types include profile, show, slot and other listed records. Use event for a dated occurrence and show only for the reusable series/template. Resolver connectivity is narrower; consult runtime catalog.

city.description: Optional city hint used to rank otherwise similar candidates.

date_hint.description: Optional date/time hint as a full RFC 3339 timestamp including time and offset. Example: 2026-07-30T20:00:00+02:00. Never pass a date-only value such as 2026-07-30.

provider.description: Optional provider namespace when query contains an identifier from that provider.

limit.description: Maximum number of ranked candidates to return; default 10.

observed_at.description: Full RFC 3339 timestamp with time and UTC offset, for example 2026-07-30T20:00:00+02:00 or 2026-07-30T18:00:00Z. Date-only values such as 2026-07-30 are invalid.

status.description: resolved only when one candidate is safe to select; ambiguous requires clarification; not_found means no candidate matched. invalid, permission_denied, and failed are typed non-success results with machine-readable error evidence.

entity_ref.description: Stable opaque reference for the candidate's canonical SR record.

entity_type.description: Canonical type of this candidate; event means one dated occurrence, show means its reusable format/template.

label.description: Human-readable candidate label containing the most useful distinguishing facts.

confidence.description: Resolver confidence from 0 to 1; not an authorization signal.

reasons.description: Compact reasons why this candidate matched the request.

summary.description: Self-contained distinguishing facts. Event candidates should include the show title, event date/time, venue, and city when available so the match can be explained without a follow-up read.

candidates.description: Ranked canonical candidates with enough facts to distinguish them.

selected_ref.description: Selected stable reference when status is resolved; otherwise null.

error_code.description: Stable machine-readable code for a typed non-success result.

message.description: Safe human-readable explanation of the typed non-success result.

error.description: Structured typed-error evidence; when present, use error.result_status for trace semantics and error.error_code for branching.

details.description: Safe machine-readable diagnostics such as missing_fields, unexpected_fields, expected_shapes, or reconciliation instructions. Never contains secrets or raw Product rows.

metadata.title: Get one Standup Republic entity
metadata.description: Read answer-ready sections of exactly one stable SR entity reference. Choose sections from the entity-type registry; source_mode defaults to canonical, compare is for bounded canonical/provider comparison, and provider_live is Admin-only where connected. subject_ref/resource_ref add an already-resolved relationship context and never replace entity_ref. The result reports source, freshness, coverage, warnings, and a typed allowed-section error for one corrected retry. Discover current entity sections via sr_runtime_health with components:['mcp'], catalog:{kind:'entity',key:'<entity_type>'}. Retired coordination entities are not part of the public plugin catalog.

employee_pages.description: Independent bounded keyset pages for EmployeeDetail current work, memberships, and activity. Applies only to sr:person refs with the detail section.

entity_type.description: Canonical SR or internal Coordination record type. Product values include application, booking, event, invoice, location, organization, payout_case, profile, show, slot, subscription, and ticket_class. Internal values include artifact, plugin_user, meeting, message, priority_item, archived project, archived task, task_proposal, attachment (legacy transfer alias), archived signal, link, coordination_event, activity_event, mcp_tool_call, and operation_run. Use priority_item for the Admin board; archived project, task, and signal references return typed retirement errors. Use artifact for private immutable R2 content or a verified Google Drive link. Use slot for one bookable lineup time window. Use event for one scheduled occurrence with a date, time, and a venue. Use show only for the reusable show format/template across occurrences; a user may colloquially say 'Show' while referring to an event.

metadata.title: Query Standup Republic entities
metadata.description: Run one bounded, versioned query profile for lists, aggregates, timelines, or reports. Read the selected profile's availability, role, scope, filter, select, grouping, and sort contract before calling; do not try guessed profiles or filter probes. Omit select when the profile publishes an answer-ready default. Use at most one supported sort, pass canonical scope_ref when available, and reuse next_cursor unchanged for the same query. Additional safe per-item Gets are usually unnecessary after a complete projection. blocked/unsupported profiles are discoverable but not callable; typed errors state the exact retry contract. Discover current profiles via sr_runtime_health with components:['mcp'], catalog:{kind:'overview'}; fetch exact filters and projection with catalog:{kind:'query',key:'<profile>'}.

profile.description: Use one exact canonical versioned profile; do not invent aliases. Read availability, filters, fields and caller-specific connectivity in the runtime catalog.

filters.description: Use the exact selected query profile filter contract from the runtime catalog; arbitrary columns are not supported.

select.description: Optional profile-specific projection. Query results contain each selected field; do not follow a complete query with per-item entity_get calls. available_slots_v1 select fields: slot_ref, event_ref, show_ref, show_title, location_ref, location_title, city, starts_at, ends_at, duration_minutes, spot_mode, availability_status, fee_eur. Omit select to receive all answer-ready fields. Use filters city, starts_after, starts_before, duration_minutes, spot_mode, and availability_status; a duration filter must be an integer number of minutes. event_inventory_v1 select fields: event_ref, show_ref, show_title, location_ref, location_title, city, starts_at, sold_quantity, capacity_quantity, remaining_quantity, latest_attempt_status, has_stale_snapshot_warning, capacity_sync_enabled, ticket_inventory_status. Omit select to receive all of these answer-ready fields. Do not use aliases such as name, label, capacity, remaining, entity_ref, tickets_sold, or remaining_capacity. open_payouts_v1 select fields: payout_case_ref, case_type, event_ref, event_title, event_starts_at, profile_ref, profile_name, amount_cents, amount_direction, currency, status, status_family, failure_code, failed_at, created_at. Omit select for the bounded default: payout_case_ref, case_type, event_ref, event_title, event_starts_at, profile_ref, amount_cents, amount_direction, currency, status, status_family, failure_code, failed_at, created_at. The response also contains summary with aggregate counts; request profile_name only when a person name is needed. Unsupported profile fields return the typed query_select_not_supported tool error.

group_by.description: Only grouping fields allowed by the selected query profile.

sort.description: Only sorting fields allowed by the selected query profile.

metadata.title: Check Standup Republic runtime health
metadata.description: Read sanitized status, freshness, last-success evidence, and bounded metrics for selected components: auth, identity, coordination, attachments, database, main_app, mcp, agent_runtime, meeting_sync, payout_pipeline, and ticketing_sync. window is a bounded lookback. detail_level=summary is available to Employee and Admin; diagnostic is Admin-only and fails closed with allowed_detail_level=summary for Employee callers. Optional catalog reads the live server registry: components:['mcp'] with catalog:{kind:'overview'} lists capabilities; kind action/query/entity and key returns exact current contracts. Use this before declaring a capability unavailable from installed plugin files. Catalog metadata is not target authorization. This tool does not expose raw logs, provider payloads, file names, or Production rows.

metadata.title: Prepare a Standup Republic action
metadata.description: Validate and freeze one registry-backed Product or internal Coordination action without mutating state. Before declaring an operation unavailable, discover the live registry via sr_runtime_health with components:['mcp'], catalog:{kind:'overview'}, then catalog:{kind:'action',key:'<operation>'} for exact payload and reference requirements. Choose operation by availability, required role, target type, confirmation_policy, use_when/not_for, required references, dependencies, and exact payload guide. A request to move, reschedule, or rebook an existing comedian between slots is booking.move with both source and destination slot refs; resolve ambiguous names through the occupied source slot and never substitute booking.remove. For Event text, the words Memo, Notiz, or Beschreibung alone are ambiguous: ask whether the user means organizer-only internal note, public customer description, or public Event title before calling Prepare. Never infer visibility from a legacy UI label. Omit legacy domain; the server derives it from operation and rejects mismatches. Invalid payloads return machine-readable missing_fields, unexpected_fields, and expected_shapes for one corrected retry. A successful Prepare returns a 48-hour manifest, opaque prepare_token, confirmation_policy, and execution_ready. For not_required operations call Execute immediately without showing a preview or asking again; required operations must wait for explicit user confirmation.

domain.description: Optional legacy hint. Prefer omitting domain: the server derives the authoritative domain from operation. If supplied, it must match the operation registry.

operation.description: Named plugin operation. Read its exact payload, availability, and confirmation policy in the runtime catalog before preparing. application.accept [active, role=employee, domain=booking]: accept one existing open application; not for rejecting or moving a booking; application.reject [active, role=employee, domain=booking]: reject one existing open application; not for accepting an application or removing a confirmed booking; batch.execute [active, role=admin, domain=admin]: freeze 2-50 related, individually valid Admin-scope actions from one clear user intent into one preview, one confirmation, and one canonical aggregate receipt; not for unrelated intents, Finance/Payment/Payout/Credential/Identity/Role/destructive/irreversible/provider-wide actions, nested batches or sessions, or pretending best-effort execution is atomic; booking.move [active, role=employee, domain=booking]: move one existing booking between two identified slots; resolve an ambiguous person through the occupied source slot before preparing; not for creating a new booking or removing and recreating a booking; booking.remove [active, role=employee, domain=booking]: remove an identified booking or occupied slot without replacing it; not for rejecting an open application or moving/rescheduling/rebooking a comedian to another slot; use booking.move with both slot refs; comedian.book [active, role=employee, domain=booking]: book one identified comedian into one identified free slot; not for creating an invitation; communication.message.acknowledge [active, role=employee, domain=coordination]: mark one received pending internal message as acknowledged; not for completing, archiving, or merely reading a message; communication.message.archive [active, role=employee, domain=coordination]: archive one message visible to the authenticated sender or recipient; not for hard-deleting message history; communication.message.complete [active, role=employee, domain=coordination]: mark one received or sent internal message as completed; not for archiving or hard-deleting it; communication.message.reply [active, role=employee, domain=coordination]: reply to one visible direct internal Coordination message; the server derives the active counterpart and canonical thread from the source message; not for external email, WhatsApp or Slack delivery; provider destinations; selecting a recipient, conversation or thread in payload; communication.message.send [active, role=employee, domain=coordination]: send one direct internal message to one active allowlisted plugin user; Prepare may be followed immediately by Execute; not for external email/WhatsApp delivery or selecting the sender in payload; coordination.artifact.create [active, role=employee, domain=coordination]: create one canonical Artifact with exactly one backing: immutable private R2 content or a link-only Google Drive file pending readonly provider verification; not for mixing R2 and Drive fields, embedding bytes, inventing provider metadata, exposing a raw R2 URL, changing Drive permissions, or bypassing linked-entity visibility; coordination.artifact.delete [active, role=employee, domain=coordination]: logically delete one owned Artifact after optimistic concurrency, active-hold and authorization checks; not for direct R2 deletion, deleting provider/meeting evidence, bypassing retention, or erasing audit/version history; coordination.artifact.grant.add [active, role=employee, domain=coordination]: grant one active allowlisted user viewer or editor access to an owned Artifact; linked-entity policy still applies independently; not for public links, team-wide implicit grants, Product role changes, or bypassing a linked entity's visibility; coordination.artifact.grant.revoke [active, role=employee, domain=coordination]: revoke one active viewer/editor grant from an owned Artifact; not for removing ownership, deleting history, or changing Project membership; coordination.artifact.link.add [active, role=employee, domain=coordination]: link one owned Artifact to an independently authorized canonical Project, Task, Message, Meeting, Signal, Run or other supported entity; not for granting visibility through the link, arbitrary URLs, or linking an entity the actor cannot access; coordination.artifact.link.remove [active, role=employee, domain=coordination]: remove one active Artifact link while preserving immutable link/audit history; not for deleting the Artifact or weakening the linked entity's own visibility policy; coordination.artifact.update [active, role=employee, domain=coordination]: optimistically update the mutable Artifact identity, title, lifecycle or retention without rewriting content versions; not for changing immutable blob/version provenance or shortening retention below an active hold; coordination.artifact.upload_finalize [active, role=employee, domain=coordination]: verify the exact reserved Artifact bytes and activate the staged immutable version; not for Google Drive Artifacts, finalizing an unknown digest, changing retention/audience, or selecting another user's Artifact; coordination.artifact.version.create [active, role=employee, domain=coordination]: append one immutable R2 content version to an editable long-lived R2 Artifact with optimistic concurrency; not for Google Drive Artifacts, rewriting an existing version, provider evidence, or retrying after a revision conflict without re-reading; coordination.priority_item.complete [active, role=admin, domain=coordination]: mark one Admin priority board card done using its current revision; not for completing an archived Coordination task or overwriting a stale board revision; coordination.priority_item.create [active, role=admin, domain=coordination]: create one Admin priority board card without an assignee or Project; not for creating an archived Coordination task, assigning a person, attaching a Project, or adding comments; coordination.priority_item.update [active, role=admin, domain=coordination]: edit one Admin priority board card using its current revision; not for editing an archived Coordination task or overwriting a stale board revision; coordination.whatsapp_history.import [active, role=admin, domain=coordination]: dry-run and, after explicit confirmation, atomically import one 1..25 item batch from one registered historical WhatsApp source with stable provider keys and immutable provenance digests; not for source parsing, unregistered chats, inferred identities or visibility, direct SQL/webhook writes, external WhatsApp sends, unbounded files, or mixing source snapshots; coordination.whatsapp_history.rollback [active, role=admin, domain=coordination]: roll back one exact applied historical WhatsApp import batch while preserving its digest-only audit evidence; not for deleting pre-existing duplicates, erasing audit receipts, rolling back a batch with derived dependencies, or broad source reset; event.bulk_metadata_update [local-only, role=employee, domain=event]: apply one category value to a frozen set of 1-200 events; not for a live filter evaluated during Execute; event.cancel [active, role=employee, domain=event]: cancel one event or its explicit future recurring scope; not for deleting a show template; event.create [active, role=employee, domain=event]: create one dated event under an existing show at an existing location; not for creating the show or location dependency; event.create_recurring [active, role=employee, domain=event]: create a bounded recurring event series for an existing show and location; not for creating a new show template; event.internal_note.set [active, role=employee, domain=event]: set or clear organizer-only internal Event notes; the user explicitly says internal or organizer-only; not for public Event copy, a public title, or ambiguous words such as Memo, Notiz, or Beschreibung without an explicit visibility; event.lineup_message.send [active, role=employee, domain=event]: send one bounded message to the current active canonical Line-up of one exact Event; not for closing or changing the Event; supplying recipient IDs, Event title, location, duration, templates, channels, provider configuration, or a free external destination; event.public_description.set [active, role=employee, domain=event]: set or clear the public Event description shown to customers; the user explicitly says public description or customer-facing text; not for organizer-only notes, the public title, or ambiguous words such as Memo, Notiz, or Beschreibung without an explicit visibility; event.public_title.set [active, role=employee, domain=event]: set or clear the Event-specific public title; the user explicitly says public title; not for the reusable Show title, public description, internal notes, or an ambiguous title request without Event scope; event.update [active, role=employee, domain=event]: change schedule, duration, or location on one identified event; not for any Event text, ticket-class, or provider-live changes; export.generate [unsupported, role=admin, domain=finance]: never in V1; explain that no private export-file surface exists; not for bounded read-only finance queries; host.set [active, role=employee, domain=booking]: set or clear host status for an identified booking or slot; not for booking a new comedian; infrastructure.capacity_schedule [local-only, role=admin, domain=admin]: schedule a bounded local Vercel-capacity simulation with mandatory auto-revert; not for calling Vercel or mutating Production infrastructure; invitation.create [active, role=employee, domain=booking]: create one open internal invitation Application for an identified profile and slot; not for directly booking the profile or claiming queued, sent, delivered, or received without the matching canonical Main App delivery stage; location.create [active, role=employee, domain=event]: create a canonical location from explicit venue data; not for creating an event at the new location in the same lifecycle; ownership_transfer.prepare [gated, role=admin, domain=finance]: request a separately approved ownership-transfer preview; not for routine payout reads; payment_account.relink [gated, role=admin, domain=finance]: request a separately approved Finance account relink; not for reading payout state; payment_account.unlink_for_reonboarding [gated, role=admin, domain=finance]: request a separately approved unlink for payment-account re-onboarding; not for routine account relinking; product_access.change_role [active, role=admin, domain=admin]: compare-and-set the canonical Product role set for one profile; not for plugin access roles; product_access.grant [gated, role=admin, domain=admin]: request a separately gated organization Product-access grant; not for plugin access; profile.editorial.update [active, role=employee, domain=booking]: update explicitly supplied comedian editorial fields through the same canonical permission as the Web comedian form; not for changing account identity, email, staff roles, payment details, or arbitrary profile columns; provider_event.create [active, role=admin, domain=ticketing]: request creation of one Eventim or Eventbrite provider event through the existing canonical Main App previewProviderEventAction/applyProviderEventAction provisioning path; not for guessing low-confidence provider matches; provider_link.remove [active, role=employee, domain=ticketing]: remove one canonical provider link from an event; not for deleting the external provider event; provider_link.set [active, role=employee, domain=ticketing]: set one exact canonical-to-provider event link; not for creating or mutating the external provider event; provider_ticketing.override_live [local-only, role=admin, domain=ticketing]: explicitly simulate a direct provider-live capacity override in the local adapter; not for canonical ticket-class configuration; use ticketing.ticket_class.update; show.create [active, role=employee, domain=event]: create one reusable show series/template; not for creating its dated event occurrences; show.create_with_events [active, role=employee, domain=event]: atomically create a new show plus a bounded event series at an existing location; not for adding events to an existing show; slot.create [active, role=employee, domain=booking]: create one bounded lineup slot on an existing event; not for booking a comedian into the slot; slot.fee.set [active, role=employee, domain=booking]: change the EUR fee of an exact frozen set of existing slots, occupied or unoccupied, with Event management permission; not for creating slots, changing Show defaults, paying invoices, or changing financially closed bookings; spot_mode.set [active, role=employee, domain=booking]: set private/public mode on a frozen set of slots; not for creating slots; ticketing.canonical_price.set [active, role=employee, domain=ticketing]: set the canonical event price in cents; not for a provider-live override; ticketing.contingent.set [active, role=employee, domain=ticketing]: set the canonical ticket contingent for one event; not for changing one ticket class; ticketing.sync.request [active, role=employee, domain=ticketing]: enqueue an idempotent canonical capacity-sync run for one future event whose capacity sync setting is enabled; not for changing sync settings or forcing a provider write when no eligible sync job can be enqueued; ticketing.sync_settings.set [active, role=employee, domain=ticketing]: change canonical price/capacity sync settings for one event; not for requesting an immediate sync run; ticketing.ticket_class.create [active, role=employee, domain=ticketing]: create a canonical SR ticket class on one event without provisioning an external Stripe product or price; not for provider-live capacity overrides or Stripe catalog provisioning; ticketing.ticket_class.update [active, role=employee, domain=ticketing]: change canonical SR ticket-class configuration; price changes are executable only while the class has no Stripe product/price IDs; payload.description: Strict operation-specific Product payload. Use the exact payload guide published on the selected operation; arbitrary SQL, URLs, code, and provider credentials are forbidden. Invalid payloads return missing_fields, unexpected_fields, and expected_shapes.

confirmation_policy.description: Server-owned registry policy. required means wait for a new explicit user confirmation before Execute; not_required means call Execute immediately after Prepare without another user turn.

execution_ready.description: True only for a prepared action whose token may be passed to Execute under its confirmation policy.

expires_at.description: Full RFC 3339 timestamp with time and UTC offset, for example 2026-07-30T20:00:00+02:00 or 2026-07-30T18:00:00Z. Date-only values such as 2026-07-30 are invalid.

details.description: Safe machine-readable diagnostics such as missing_fields, unexpected_fields, expected_shapes, or reconciliation instructions. Never contains secrets or raw Product rows.

error.description: Machine-readable evidence for a typed non-success result. result_status matches the correlated observer trace; retryable never implies that an action is safe to replay with a different idempotency key.

metadata.title: Execute a prepared Standup Republic action
metadata.description: Execute exactly one previously prepared active action after authorization and state revalidation. If Prepare returned confirmation_policy=required, call only after explicit user confirmation; if it returned not_required, call immediately without another user turn. Pass the exact opaque prepare_token plus a caller-generated stable 16-128 character idempotency_key using letters, digits, dot, underscore, tilde, or hyphen; never use manifest_ref as the idempotency key, and likewise never use prepare_token, receipt_ref, or another sr: reference. Reuse the same key only for a retry of the same execution. A succeeded action proves only the operation's canonical internal contract: requested proves durable Main App outbox acceptance only; claim provider acceptance only from post_check.external_effects state provider_accepted, sending only from sent, delivery only from delivered, and reading only from read, each with canonical evidence. Explicitly state not_requested_by_policy, requested, queued, processing, provider_unknown, failed, or unknown; never paraphrase them as sent, delivered, received, published, shared, or successfully dispatched. For an unknown transport outcome, reconcile operation_run_ref with sr_entity_get sections status, receipt, and post_check; never blind-retry with a new key. Gated, blocked, local-only, and unsupported operations remain non-executable in Production.

prepare_token.description: Opaque prepare_token returned by the exact sr_action_prepare call being confirmed. Do not use manifest_ref instead.

idempotency_key.description: Caller-generated stable retry key for this one confirmed execution: 16-128 characters using only letters, digits, dot, underscore, tilde, or hyphen. Example: gp041-show-create-20260723. Reuse the same key only when retrying the same execution. Never copy manifest_ref, prepare_token, receipt_ref, or any sr:... reference into this field.

observed_at.description: Full RFC 3339 timestamp with time and UTC offset, for example 2026-07-30T20:00:00+02:00 or 2026-07-30T18:00:00Z. Date-only values such as 2026-07-30 are invalid.

replayed.description: True only when this response replays the already committed canonical receipt for the same prepare token and idempotency key; no second mutation ran.

details.description: Safe machine-readable diagnostics such as missing_fields, unexpected_fields, expected_shapes, or reconciliation instructions. Never contains secrets or raw Product rows.

error.description: Machine-readable evidence for a typed non-success result. result_status matches the correlated observer trace; retryable never implies that an action is safe to replay with a different idempotency key.
